principles:
**The shared requirement.** *A credential that is live at merge time must not reach the default branch without a server-side check failing first.* Source: ledger row F050 (`docs/port/COMMONALITY.md:56`), realized in py by `.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` at pin `b08bccfb` (read through the pin, 2026-09-10; reproduced in full in the evidence log, section 01).

**Agreement level: capability and policy — not tool, not configuration.** The three repositories must agree that a non-bypassable CI-tier check exists and that it fails on a validated credential. They need not agree on which binary produces that verdict, because the scanner is an executed build tool: it enters no repository's public API and no repository's dependency graph.

| Must agree (capability and policy) | May vary (ecosystem-local) |
|---|---|
| A CI-tier job exists that fails on a live credential | Which scanner binary produces the verdict |
| The verdict is server-side and a contributor cannot skip it | How the binary reaches the runner (Action, container, release tarball) |
| The job runs on `pull_request` and on `push` to `main` | Whether the scan is diff-scoped or full-history |
| The failure is a check that branch-protection rules can require | Which runner OS the single scan job lands on (R11 owns this) |

**Essential behaviors.** (1) Scan the content a pull request would add, and the history already present. (2) Attempt live validation against the issuing provider and distinguish verified from candidate. (3) **Fail the gate when a verified credential is present, and fail it when the scanner produced no verdict at all** — with the TruffleHog CLI the workflow allow-lists the tool's documented exit codes rather than testing the exit's sign, in a step whose shell cannot mask the scanner's status (the rule and its conditions are stated in full in Part 2: `0` passes, `183` and `1` fail, any code outside the documented set fails as a tool error; `--fail` and `--fail-on-scan-errors` are both passed; the code is captured, the step declares `shell: bash` with the scanner out of an unguarded pipe, and the report is an additional condition rather than a substitute). `--fail` has to be passed because without it a verified finding leaves the process at `0` — `183` is documented as returned "only … if `--fail` flag is used" (`06a`, `06b`); `--fail-on-scan-errors` has to be passed because a non-fatal scan error otherwise also leaves it at `0` (executed: `07g`–`07j`); and the shell condition is not optional, because under the default `run:` shell a piped scanner hands the allow-list a `0` it did not earn and the job passes unscanned (executed in revision 6, section 12). (4) Name the finding's location without printing the secret — this tool has **no** `--redact`, executed by invoking the binary with that flag and asserting its refusal on both source kinds against an accepted-flag control (`08e`, `08f`), so the behavior is obtained from the output format instead: `--github-actions` emits one `::warning file=…,line=…` annotation per finding and writes zero occurrences, on stdout and stderr, of each of the three fixture values this scanner detects, asserted one value at a time (`08c`, `08h`–`08j`), where the default and `--json` formats write them verbatim (`08a`, `08b`). The fixture's fourth value is not detected at this pin and carries no such claim (`08g`, `08k`). (5) Require no vendor account and no paid licence key.

**Observable acceptance criteria**, each labelled by what has actually been run:

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A committed, non-live but realistic credential (a well-formed PAT-shaped string, an `AKIA`-shaped key pair, a `postgres://user:password@localhost/db` URI in `.env.example`) leaves the gate green, so no exclusion file is needed | **Executed** — `--only-verified --fail` on that fixture exits `0` (`07a`), while the *same scan* without the filter exits `183` on two unverified matches (`07b`), which is what shows the filter and not an absence of matches is doing the work |
| 2 | A credential present only in history (committed, then deleted) is still found with no `--since-commit` flag | **Executed** — a two-commit fixture whose working tree is empty: unfiltered `--fail` exits `183` having scanned the deleted blob (`07c`), and `--only-verified` passes it (`07d`) |
| 3 | A genuinely live credential fails the gate, naming file and line, at the documented code | **Executed against the tool, not against a workflow** — TruffleHog's own published corpus `trufflesecurity/test_keys` yields two findings the issuing providers confirm (detectors `AWS` and `URI`) and exits `183` under `--only-verified --fail` (`09a`); `--github-actions` names file and line (`08c`) and writes zero occurrences of every detected fixture value, on stdout and on stderr (`08h`–`08j`). What remains P03's is the same outcome *inside a GitHub Actions job on a pull request* |
| 4 | The first push to a new repository created from the template runs cleanly | **Executed for the failure it guards against** — that failure is the Action's equal-base/head guard, and the CLI has none: a repository with exactly one commit scans to exit `0` with zero `BASE and HEAD commits are the same` errors (`07e`). The workflow-level run remains P03's |
| 5 | **A scan step whose scanner cannot run, or which scans nothing, fails the job — including when the step's shell could hide it.** Run the real workflow with the scan deliberately broken in each of four ways — the binary replaced by `false` or its path pointed at a nonexistent file; a rejected flag added; a scan target that does not exist; and any of those with the scan command piped into `tee` or `jq` — and assert the job fails in all four, not passes | **Proposed, not executed as a workflow** — no workflow exists yet, so a hosted runner's behaviour is P03's to prove. What *is* executed here is the documented set and every code eleven invocations produced (`06a`, `07f`–`07k`), including the two paths on which this tool exits `0` having scanned nothing; the shell half was executed in revision 6 under both shells GitHub documents (`12a`–`12h`) |

**The py split, verified at the pinned tag — what it does and does not establish.** The Opus raw's load-bearing finding is that py's diff-scan-on-PR / full-scan-on-push split is a workaround for the incumbent Action's error when base and head are equal, not an independent requirement. I verified it rather than accepting it, and it holds, at this width:

- py's own comment names the tool error as the reason for the conditional: "on push (esp. a new repo's FIRST push) base==head, which TruffleHog rejects ('BASE and HEAD commits are the same')" (`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml`, at pin `b08bccfb`, evidence log section 01).
- The error exists in the tool's own action definition at **`v3.95.9`, the exact tag py pins**: `if [ "$base_commit" == "$head_commit" ] ; then echo "::error::BASE and HEAD commits are the same…"; exit 1; fi` (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/v3.95.9/action.yml`, sha256 `c3847cdb…`, retrieved 2026-09-10; executed in revision 6, evidence log section 03, and not re-fetched in this revision).
- The same file shows the guard is reached **only when the workflow supplies a non-empty `base` or `head`**, and that the Action's own `else` branch derives the range from the event, including the all-zeros first push. So the split is a consequence of how py drives the Action, not a property of secret scanning.

What this changes about the item: the diff/full split is **not** part of the shared requirement and does not have to be ported. What it does **not** license is the stronger claim that only a different tool can drop it — py's own push path already passes an empty `base`, which produces a full-history scan through the same Action, so **single-mode full-history is achievable with either tool**; what the recommendation buys is dropping the two conditional GitHub expressions, which either tool permits. Kingfisher additionally has no equal-commit guard at all: omitting `--since-commit` scans full history (`docs/USAGE.md:598-605,644`, retrieved 2026-09-10; and executed as acceptance criterion 2 above).

**What the owner's ruling adds to that paragraph, executed at this revision's pin.** The sentence above is about the Action and about Kingfisher, and both halves stand; the tool the ruling selects needed its own check. The TruffleHog **CLI** has no equal-commit guard either — the guard lives in `action.yml`, not in the binary — and a repository with exactly one commit, which is the shape of a template's first push, scans to exit `0` with zero `BASE and HEAD commits are the same` errors (`07e`). Its full-history behaviour with no `--since-commit` is executed too (`07c`). The ruling's stated reason for preferring the CLI over py's Action form — that the Action is `docker`-based, `ubuntu-latest`-only and carries the first-push failure — therefore holds on primary evidence in all three parts.

**Architectural alternatives, compared before any tool was weighed.**

| # | Architecture | Gives | Costs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | No dedicated workflow; rely on GitHub native scanning plus the R39 hook tier | zero workflow code; matches 10 of 10 surveyed Rust projects | no coverage in private clones; no required status check for R12; the hook tier is bypassable with `--no-verify` | rejected — fails the requirement in private clones |
| B | A third-party vendor Action (`uses:`) wrapping a scanner | one `uses:` line; the vendor maintains the glue | inherits the Action's runtime constraints and licence terms | rejected on evidence, not preference, and the owner's ruling W0-R17b rejects py's Action form on the same grounds: TruffleHog's Action ends in `docker run` (verified at `v3.95.9`, revision 6's evidence log section 03) and `gitleaks/gitleaks-action` requires a purchased `GITLEAKS_LICENSE` key for organizations, which is vendor onboarding and is what that exclusion rests on — **executed at a pinned README commit in this revision, lines 43 and 75** (`11a`, `11b`), after round 6 found revision 6's pattern could not match the file it cited; its `NOASSERTION` licence field is recorded as observed but is not a ground, because the owner's ruling of 2026-09-12 stops licence compatibility being evaluated at all (`11c`) |
| C | Install a pinned scanner binary in a `run:` step and invoke the CLI | control of flags, exit-code handling and version pin; provenance verifiable before execution, subject to the two qualification paragraphs below | roughly eight extra workflow lines, plus an explicit version-refresh path because Dependabot does not track a version inside a `run:` step | **recommended, and the form the owner's ruling directs** |
| D | Reuse R39's hook-tier scanner at CI tier too | one tool to learn and update | no detector diversity; and F050's row note currently requires distinct tools | possible; see the `BASELINE-REVIEW:` below |

**Shape C's safety advantage over shape B, restated for the tool the owner's ruling selects, because the two candidates publish different provenance and revision 6's paragraph described Kingfisher's. This paragraph and the next state the qualification once in full; every later mention of provenance verification in this document carries them.** **TruffleHog publishes no GitHub build attestation**, so `gh attestation verify` — the one-command check revision 6 relied on — does not apply: run against the pinned tarball with a declared token it fails, GitHub's attestations endpoint answering `HTTP 404` for that artifact's digest, and no attestation output is written (`04g`, asserted as the *absence*, so the assertion fails if TruffleHog ever starts publishing one). What the release does publish is a `checksums.txt` signed by Sigstore keyless signing, and that is what is executed here: the downloaded `trufflehog_3.97.4_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` has sha256 `57e2a41c…`, equal to the entry for that file in the published `checksums.txt` (`04a`); the accompanying certificate's subject-alternative-name URI is `https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v3.97.4` and its issuer is `O=sigstore.dev, CN=sigstore-intermediate` (`04b`, `04c`); and the published signature over `checksums.txt` verifies against that certificate's public key — `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` prints `Verified OK` — while a copy of the file with one byte changed fails verification, which is the negative control that makes the positive result evidence (`04d`, `04e`). Unlike `gh attestation verify`, none of this needs a GitHub token. A tag-pinned third-party Action offers no equivalent artifact-level check at all.

**What the executed verification does NOT establish, stated in full here because two earlier revisions of this document overstated a provenance check and were rejected for it.** `openssl dgst -verify` checks one thing: that the signature was produced by the private key matching the certificate this release published. It validates **no chain** from that certificate to the Sigstore root, and it checks **no Rekor transparency-log inclusion** — so on its own it does not exclude a certificate that never came from Fulcio. The command that does both is `cosign verify-blob --certificate <pem> --signature <sig> --certificate-identity https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v3.97.4 --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com trufflehog_3.97.4_checksums.txt`, and **cosign is not installed on this host, so that assertion is a named `SKIP` and never a pass** (`04h`) — the R49 discipline, under which a skip cannot stand in for a check that passed. Whether cosign is present on, or installable into, a GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest` runner is **not** asserted here in either direction; it is in the unproven table above as P03's. Two further properties of the certificate are worth recording so no reader misreads the log: its validity window is ten minutes wide, because Sigstore keyless certificates are ephemeral and bound to the signing event rather than to a period a verifier waits inside — an expired window is not a failure — and the SAN URI is *read from* the certificate rather than *enforced* by any flag this check passes, exactly as revision 6 recorded for the attestation's `buildSignerURI`. Enforcing it is what `--certificate-identity` above does, and P03's install step passes it. **What section 04 establishes is a developer-machine fact, not a CI fact.** No GitHub Actions job has verified this release for this template — none exists yet — so the install shape's dependence on provenance verification being available in CI is a requirement on the implementation phase, recorded in the unproven table above and in the migration implications below, not a settled fact here.

**The provenance command revision 6 used was environment-dependent, and two revisions of this document recorded one of its prerequisites as though it were not — that is the defect revision 2 repaired and the defect revision 5 repaired. The diagnosis is kept, and it is still load-bearing, because this revision runs that same command as the check that TruffleHog publishes no attestation (`04g`).** `gh attestation verify` builds its Sigstore verifier from TUF trusted-root metadata that it refreshes into `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/gh/.sigstore` (default `$HOME/.cache/gh/.sigstore`). Three prerequisites must hold, or the command fails before it looks at the artifact at all: **(1) that cache path must be writable**, or gh exits `1` printing `error creating Sigstore verifier: no valid Sigstore verifiers could be initialized`; **(2) `gh` must be authenticated**, since unauthenticated it refuses — a non-zero exit, gh's own remedy `gh auth login` on stderr, and no attestation output — at gh's documented authentication exit code, observed `4` at `gh version 2.98.0 (2026-08-20)`; **(3) the host must reach** `api.github.com`, `tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev` and `tuf-repo.github.com`. All three were executed as controls in **revision 6**, whose assertion labels are its own and are cited as such: the unwritable cache at `07f`, the refusal triple at `07h`, the resolved binary being the gh CLI rather than a version-manager launcher at `07g`, and the refusal's code asserted against that binary's own `gh help exit-codes` topic at `07i` — all in `review/evidence/secret-scanning-ci-workflow-r6-repo.log`, which this revision does not re-execute. **This revision depends on prerequisites (2) and (3) only**, because `04g` needs the command to reach GitHub and be refused for *want of an attestation* rather than for want of a login: it therefore runs under a declared token and redirects the trusted-root cache into the script's own working directory, exactly as revision 6 did, and with no declared token it `SKIP`s by name rather than passing on an ambient login. Each prerequisite is recorded this way because each has already been recorded the other way and failed to reproduce: revision 1's check inherited the caller's `$HOME`, so it passed in a permissive shell and then failed, exit `1`, under the revision-1 audit's sandbox, whose writes were confined to the workspace and `$TMPDIR` (`review/audit-codex.r1.md`, finding F1); revision 4's authentication control asserted the bare number `4` from whatever `gh` `PATH` resolved, so it failed, exit `1`, under the revision-4 audit, whose `PATH` put a `mise` shim ahead of the gh CLI (`review/audit-codex.r4.md`, finding F1); and revision 5 satisfied the authentication prerequisite from the caller's ambient `gh` login without declaring it, which the revision-5 audit rejected as finding F2 (`review/audit-codex.md`). This revision's script keeps every one of those repairs: it exports its own empty `$HOME`, resolves the gh CLI by probing rather than by `PATH` order and rejects launchers outright, and takes its credential only from a declared token.

**How the selected design preserves each principle.** *Non-bypassable server-side verdict*: the job runs on GitHub-hosted infrastructure on both triggers, so a contributor's `--no-verify` cannot reach it. *Fails on a live credential and not on a fake one*: `--only-verified` — a hidden flag at this pin that sets the tool's `--results` selection to `verified` alone, read in `main.go` at `v3.97.4` and asserted (`06d`), and accepted by the shipped binary where an invented flag is rejected (`06e`) — keeps only provider-confirmed findings, and both halves are executed: the template-shaped fake credentials pass the gate under it (`07a`) while the same scan without it fails at `183` (`07b`), and TruffleHog's own published corpus of verifiable credentials fails the gate at `183` with two provider-confirmed findings (`09a`). The gate allow-lists the documented codes — `0` passes, `183` and `1` fail, any other code fails as a tool error — rather than reading the exit's sign, in a step that passes `--fail` and `--fail-on-scan-errors`, captures the code, declares `shell: bash`, keeps the scanner out of an unguarded pipe, and treats the report as an additional condition.
